correctness.rationale: All required metric inequalities follow from 2t>=1. Full-dimensional polar duality reduces facets to connected tight-edge graphs. If exterior values attain a distance one then all exterior values are binary and every core tight component must meet 0 or 1; otherwise all exterior values coincide, sign reversal gives a single exterior level and every core component must meet the opposite endpoint. Tight paths anchored at endpoints force the four-symbol core state set for 1/2<t<1 and three symbols at t=1/2. Exact exhaustive 4^4 feasibility and graph connectivity yield A,B=(38,27) or (26,15), hence A(2^(N-4)-2)+2B. Equilateral t=1 gives 2^N-2. The independent spanning-tree enumeration verifies all small cases without being used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-dimensional facet classification for the smallest natural cyclic overlapping-short-edge core, which is neither matching-decomposable nor tree-like. It reveals two different sharp boundary collapses (triangle-saturation and loss of edge distinction) and strict facet inflation throughout an open parameter interval, quantitatively illuminating nongeneric transitions in Lipschitz-free ball geometry. It is not a mere substitution of known matching formulas.
